If your project has its own `<Button>`, a plain `<button>` skips its styles, its loading state, and its tracking. This rule reports the elements you list, so that everyone uses the replacement.

Nothing is forbidden until you fill in `forbid`. Both JSX and `React.createElement()` are checked.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"options": [{"forbid": ["button"]}]} */}
```jsx
<button onClick={save}>Save</button>;
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"forbid": ["button"]}]} */}
```js
React.createElement("button", { onClick: save }, "Save");
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"options": [{"forbid": ["button"]}]} */}
```jsx
<Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>;
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/forbid-elements" = ["error", { forbid = ["marquee", { element = "button", message = "use our Button component" }] }]
```

The one option is `forbid`, a list that is empty by default. An entry is the name of an element, or an object:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `element` | The name, as it is written in the tag: `"button"`, `"Modal"`, `"legacy.Modal"`. |
| `message` | Added to the report: `<button> is forbidden, use our Button component`. |

{/* bad {"count": 2, "options": [{"forbid": ["legacy.Modal", {"element": "button", "message": "use our Button component"}]}]} */}
```jsx
<legacy.Modal>
  <button>Close</button>
</legacy.Modal>;
```
